title: Object-Oriented Pattern (Luau Classes)
summary: Build classes with metatables: a class table with __index pointing at itself, a .new() constructor returning setmetatable'd instances, and methods defined with colon syntax.

details.heading: How method lookup works
details.body: instance:method() → look up 'method' on instance → miss → __index redirects to Class → found. Instance fields shadow class fields; class fields act as shared defaults.

details.heading: Single inheritance
details.body: Set the subclass's metatable `__index` to the superclass (or to a table whose __index chains up). Luau type checking understands this with `typeof()` annotations.

explanation.whatItIs: Luau has no built-in class keyword, but metatables give you the standard pattern: a class table acts as both namespace and method store, and instances are tables wired to fall back to it.
explanation.whyItExists: Games model *things* — enemies, pets, vehicles, inventory slots. Classes let each thing carry its own data while sharing behavior code.
whenToUse: Many similar objects with their own state: enemies, projectiles, pets
State machines and controllers that own update loops
whenNotToUse: One-off scripts — a module of functions is simpler
Data-only records — a plain table is enough
Don't build deep inheritance trees; prefer composition (objects holding other objects)
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Class (methods live here)
  ↑ __index fallback
Instance (fields live here: health, position, ...)

obj:method()
   → obj.method? no
   → Class.method? yes → call with self = obj
```
tips: Keep constructors the only place that creates instances
Use type annotations: `export type Enemy = typeof(setmetatable({} :: EnemyFields, Enemy))`
A :Destroy() method cleaning up connections/instances mirrors Roblox's own API style
commonMistakes: Calling `Class.method(obj)` mixed with `obj:method()` inconsistently — pick colon style
Storing per-instance state on the CLASS table — all instances then share it
Forgetting cleanup: instances holding event connections leak

examples.title: A complete Enemy class
examples.code:
local Enemy = {}
Enemy.__index = Enemy

function Enemy.new(model)
    local self = setmetatable({}, Enemy)
    self.model = model
    self.health = 100
    self.connection = model.PrimaryPart.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
        self:onTouched(hit)
    end)
    return self
end

function Enemy:onTouched(hit)
    local humanoid = hit.Parent and hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if humanoid then
        humanoid:TakeDamage(10)
    end
end

function Enemy:takeDamage(amount)
    self.health -= amount
    if self.health <= 0 then
        self:destroy()
    end
end

function Enemy:destroy()
    if self.connection then self.connection:Disconnect() end
    self.model:Destroy()
end

return Enemy

-- Usage (server Script):
-- local Enemy = require(script.Parent.Enemy)
-- local goblin = Enemy.new(workspace.Goblin)
examples.whyItWorks: Each Enemy instance owns its model, health, and touch connection. Behavior (onTouched, takeDamage) lives once on the class.
examples.commonMistake: Skipping destroy() leaks the Touched connection forever — always pair constructors with cleanup.
